headline: MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty resigns following PM's directive over Radda health center attack
summary: The reserved women's seat MP submitted her resignation after the Prime Minister's firm instruction, prompted by the demolition and looting of a healthcare facility in Mirpur.
details: Reserved women's seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty has resigned following a directive from the Prime Minister. This action comes in the wake of an attack on the Radda MCH-FP Center, a private healthcare facility in Mirpur.

The incident involved the demolition and looting of the mother and child health service institution on September 24. Local BNP politicians were implicated in the attack, leading to widespread criticism.

Upon returning from the UN General Assembly, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman took a strong stance on recent social crimes involving party members. The Radda incident was a key focus, prompting the directive for Misty's resignation.

Misty submitted her resignation letter to National Parliament Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad yesterday afternoon, and her seat was declared vacant shortly after. This move is seen as a clear message from the Prime Minister against misconduct.

The Radda incident is not isolated; there have been growing concerns about law and order since the fall of the Sheikh Hasina government. Allegations of land grabbing, extortion, attacks, vandalism, and political influence have surfaced across the country.

In addition to Misty's resignation, the BNP and its affiliated organizations have taken further disciplinary actions. Dhaka Metropolitan North committees of BNP and Jubo Dal, and Dhaka Metropolitan West committee of Chhatra Dal, were dissolved.

Furthermore, 14 individuals from various levels of BNP, Chhatra Dal, Swechchasebak Dal, and Sramik Dal have been expelled from their respective organizations. These decisions were made amid discussions of local BNP leaders' involvement in the Radda incident.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi stated that anyone violating party discipline or engaging in unethical activities will not be spared. This underscores the party's commitment to accountability.

High-level sources from the Prime Minister's Office confirmed that the PM gathered information and consulted advisors on the Radda incident. Recommendations for exemplary organizational and legal action were given, highlighting the government's embarrassment over the event.

headline_marked: 13-year-old student's [[leg broken by teacher]] in Meherpur madrasa
headline: 13-year-old student's leg broken by teacher in Meherpur madrasa
summary: A student at Fazlul Ulum Qawmi Madrasa was allegedly beaten with a bamboo stick for failing to memorize his lessons, resulting in a bone fracture.
details: A 13-year-old student named Shoeb Ali has allegedly had his leg broken after being beaten by a teacher at Fazlul Ulum Qawmi Madrasa in Gangni, Meherpur.
The victim, a resident of West Malshadah village, stated that teacher Din Islam beat him with a bamboo stick because he could not recite his lessons.
Shoeb's father, Abdul Goni, initially did not realize the severity of the injury, but took his son to the Gangni Upazila Health Complex on Thursday after the boy became unable to walk.
Medical Officer Dr. Samia Sultana confirmed that the student suffered a fracture in the ankle area and is currently receiving treatment at the hospital.
When contacted, teachers from the madrasa declined to comment on the allegations.
Gangni Police Station OC Muhaddid Morshed Chowdhury stated that necessary legal action will be taken once a written complaint is filed.
